//: The editor's half of the tokenizer. Every value here is the same rule the
parser holds, said in the one dialect VSCode understands.
FOUR SPACES, everywhere. Ruled 2026-09-09 ('four everywhere'), and it is
one constant in the printer too (`script.zig`'s `indent_canon`) rather
than one per site, because two names for one value is an invitation to
drift apart. The value itself lives in package.json's
`configurationDefaults` — that is the only place VSCode reads a tab size
from — and this file carries the rules that decide WHEN to add one.

comments.//: `//` opens a comment; `#` does NOT — ruled 2026-08-25, because `#` is the tag sigil (`#garrison`) and cannot also lead a comment. rill has no block comment, so none is declared: an editor that offers one would be offering a syntax error.

//wordPattern: A word is what the tokenizer calls one, and nothing else:
`:k`      a fold reference, sigil included, ONE token (§3.10)
`$wind`   a field channel, sigil included, ONE token
`-` and `/` are name-INTERIOR when they JOIN two name
should take all of it, because that is one name.
`250ms`   a duration is a number glued to a unit, one token
The dot is deliberately NOT in the pattern. `plane.drift.@self.k.tight`
is five words, so a double-click takes the segment under the cursor —
which is the one you are about to retype. Taking the whole path was the
other reading and was rejected: it makes the common edit harder to serve
the rare one, and Ctrl+D on `k` across a file is worth more than one

//: Indent after the four things that open a body: a def signature's `=`,
the `) =` that closes a WRAPPED signature, a `describe` head, and any
unclosed opener. Outdent on a closer.
The `) =` alternative arrived with the width canon (2026-09-09). A
signature that runs past 88 columns is printed one port per line and
closes in the left margin, so the `=` that used to sit on the `def`
line now sits on a line beginning with `)`. Without this the body of
every wrapped definition lands in the left margin — and it is the
shape `kernels/roaches.rill` is printed in.
That line matches BOTH patterns, which is right and not a conflict:
the `)` dedents back to the `def`'s own column, and the `=` indents
the body under it.
`[{\[(]\s*$` already covered the other two wrapped forms — an open
`(` at end of line is a wrapping signature and an open `[` is a
wrapping array — which is why they need nothing new here.
Continue a `//` comment onto the next line. Not a nicety here:
`matryoshka/kernels/roaches.rill` is the documented exemplar and is
roughly four-fifths prose — the numbers, the traps and the reasoning
all live in `//` lines. Writing that by hand without this is typing
two slashes a hundred and forty times.
A leading `|` continues the statement above it — no statement can
begin with a pipe, so it has never had a second meaning
(parser.zig:1905). Enter after one keeps the pipe in the same
column, which since the width canon (2026-09-09) is the printer's:
a broken chain is one stage per line at indent 4, `|` first.
It holds from the SECOND continuation on. The first one is typed
after an ordinary statement line, and no lexical rule can tell a
statement that is about to be continued from one that is finished —
so that one is the author's Tab, or the formatter's on save. Better
than the alternative, which is indenting after every statement in
the file on the chance that a `|` follows.
